title: fzf-tmux rendered incomplete borders
body: - [x] I have read through the manual page (`man fzf`) - [x] I have the latest version of fzf - [x] I have searched through the existing issues ## Info - OS - [ ] Linux - [x] Mac OS X - [ ] Windows - [ ] Etc. - Shell - [ ] bash - [x] zsh - [ ] fish ## Problem / Steps to reproduce ```shell ls | fzf-tmux -p ```

comments.body:

* Or setting `RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN` environment variable to 0 or 1.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hmm, that's strange. Not sure why the variable is not propagated in your setup.

Well then, we can explicitly pass the variable like so in `fzf-tmux` script. Does this help in your case?

```diff
diff --git a/bin/fzf-tmux b/bin/fzf-tmux
index e891b78..ed255fc 100755
--- a/bin/fzf-tmux
+++ b/bin/fzf-tmux
@@ -192,6 +192,7 @@ if [[ "$opt" =~ "-E" ]]; then
 fi
 [[ -n "$FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS"    ]] && envs="$envs FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS=$(printf %q "$FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS")"
 [[ -n "$FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND" ]] && envs="$envs FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND=$(printf %q "$FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND")"
+[[ -n "$RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN" ]] && envs="$envs RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN=$(printf %q "$RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN")"
 [[ -n "$BAT_THEME" ]] && envs="$envs BAT_THEME=$(printf %q "$BAT_THEME")"
 echo "$envs;" > "$argsf"
 
```

comments.body: > ```diff > [[ -n "$RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN" ]] && envs="$envs RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN=$(printf %q "$RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN")" > ``` This actually works. Thanks @participant1
